health_and_wellness.summary: Prioritizes steady, moderate health maintenance through hiking, low-impact yoga, balance class, home cooking, meditation, conventional medicine, and vaccination.

Uses meditation, breathing exercises, yoga, and occasional supportive alternative approaches but does not replace medical care with them (Q37, Q50).
Does not smoke, drinks modestly at about two or three drinks per week, does not use marijuana or other substances, and is cautious about pain medication dependence (Q38, Q39).
Maggie has had thyroid issues and a hip replacement, sister Elaine has diabetes, and friends help one another with appointments and health check-ins (Q35).

summaries.demographer: Andrew Black is a 70-year-old White, non-Hispanic man living in Payson, Arizona, with his wife Margaret "Maggie" Black (Q51, Q84, Q88, Q89). He was born in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, in 1955, lived there at age 16, and comes from a stable two-parent Midwestern household with a younger sister (Q85, Q87, Q97, Q98, Q99). He has some college and a drafting certificate but no bachelor's degree, and he is retired from carpentry/cabinetmaking/residential drafting (Q90, Q65). His household is economically stable through Social Security, Maggie's pension, retirement savings, Medicare, and a paid-off home, though he remains cautious about medical and long-term-care costs (Q58, Q74, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Andrew shows strong planning habits, loss aversion around retirement security, and a preference for stability over status, visible in choosing craft autonomy over a steadier architectural office path and later paying off his home before retirement (Q02, Q83). He budgets carefully, delays discretionary purchases when expenses rise, and preserves emergency savings rather than borrowing (Q60, Q61, Q82). His spending reflects identity-consistent utility: art supplies, camera gear, modest travel, family gifts, and community giving matter more than consumption or luxury (Q57, Q62, Q64). He responds to uncertainty through routines, diversification of income sources, and practical preparation for health, fire season, vehicle maintenance, and home repairs (Q59, Q62, Q83).
summaries.political_scientist: Andrew is a regular voter and self-described Independent who leans Democratic, especially in national politics, while still evaluating local candidates individually (Q23, Q95, Q96). His political identity combines Midwestern thrift and localism with support for civil rights, public education, environmental conservation, voting access, health care access, democratic institutions, and public accountability (Q24, Q25, Q27). He trusts expertise selectively, relying on doctors and public health sources for medical information and rejecting outrage-based media (Q42). His views on race and policing have become more reflective since Black Lives Matter, with conversation, reading, and modest donations rather than protest participation (Q26, Q29, Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Andrew presents as conscientious, reflective, calm, and craft-oriented, with identity organized around fidelity, curiosity, care, usefulness, and attention (Q01, Q65, Q109). He regulates stress through structured routines, walking, writing, meditation, making things, limiting news, and talking with Maggie rather than substances or social media venting (Q38, Q43, Q45, Q49, Q50). His cognitive style is spatial, narrative, and philosophical: he connects carpentry, landscape, photography, memoir, and phenomenological reflection into a coherent self-concept (Q02, Q17, Q47, Q108). Relationally, he favors small stable ties, dependable family contact, intergenerational mentoring, and careful listening over broad social exposure (Q05, Q06, Q07, Q46).
